2.2.3. Foreign Policy Behavior: Patterns and Trends

Foreign policy behavior refers to the actions states take towards each other. It is important to note that these actions usually are not as ends in themselves, but are tied in some way with larger purposes, from long range objectives to short term objectives that leaders hope to achieve in their dealings with other countries. The nature of foreign policy is such that one can expect to find double standards and inconsistencies in the records of all countries. It is not easy to label countries as simply peace loving or war-like or to use other such categorizations.

Nevertheless, patterns of foreign policy behavior can be identified. Arnold Wolfers, a famous specialist in the field of International Relations, suggested that all foreign policy behavior ultimately boils down to three possible patterns:

  1. Self-preservation: Maintaining the status quo.
  2. Self-extension: Revising the status quo in one’s own favor.
  3. Self-abnegation: Revising the status quo in some else’s favor.

Detailed Analysis of Patterns:
Seen from the above perspective, the foreign policy patterns of countries such as the United States can be categorized as self-preservation. United States, following World War II emerged as one of the strongest actors and superpowers in international relations. The international institutions (IMF, World Bank, GATT/WTO) that were established following Second World War have been strongly shaped by the United States. The underlying philosophy of such institutions, and even the decision-making procedures are all shaped to serve the global interests of the country. Even the United Nations has been serving the interest of the United States as the country has a key position in the Security Council as one of the Veto powers. Cognizant of all the advantages that accrue from the existing international system and international economic order, the U.S. has become the staunch supporter of the international order. Any attempt to reform the international system and the politico-economic order will face strong criticisms, if not threat or use of force, and sanctions. These days U.S. has become the sole defender of the international system and the liberal economic-political order after the collapse of USSR and decline of communist ideology.

On the other hand, newly emerging powers such as China, India, Brazil, Germany, and others are competing to restructure the international institutions and different regimes so as to create an enabling environment to promote their national interest. Such policy trends can be equated with Wolfers’ model of self-extension.

The third model, i.e. self-abnegation, reflects the foreign policy trends that are being displayed in Less Developing Countries (LDCs). This can be seen in the weak states of the world which fail to defend and promote their national interests in their external relations. States that are weak and very much dependent on foreign aid are profoundly caught with many problems in order to pursue an autonomous policy. Such countries may succumb to such challenges and compromise their long-lasting national interest for temporary and immediate benefits.

የሃገራት የውጭ ፖሊሲ ባህሪ (Foreign Policy Behavior): ሀገራት እርስ በርሳቸው የሚያደርጉት ድርጊትና ግንኙነት ነው። ይህ ድርጊት በራሱ መጨረሻ (end) ሳይሆን የረጅም እና የአጭር ጊዜ ብሄራዊ ጥቅሞቻቸውን ለማሳካት የሚጠቀሙበት መንገድ ነው። የአለም ሀገራት የውጭ ፖሊሲ ሁሌም ወጥ ላይሆን ይችላል (double standards እና inconsistency ይታይበታል)።

ታዋቂው የ IR ምሁር Arnold Wolfers የሀገራትን የውጭ ፖሊሲ ባህሪ በ 3 ዋና ዋና ዘይቤዎች (Patterns) ይከፍለዋል፦

  • 1. Self-preservation (ያለውን ሁኔታ ማስቀጠል/Status Quo)፦ ሀገራት አሁን ያለው አለምአቀፍ ስርአት ስለሚጠቅማቸው እንዳይቀየር ይከላከላሉ።
    ምሳሌ፦ አሜሪካ (USA) ከሁለተኛው የዓለም ጦርነት በኋላ IMF, World Bank, WTO እና UN Security Council ላይ ያላትን የቪቶ (Veto) ስልጣን በመጠቀም አሁን ያለውን የካፒታሊዝም/ሊበራል ስርአት እንዳይቀየር ታስከብራለች።
  • 2. Self-extension (ስርአቱን ለራስ ጥቅም መቀየር)፦ አዳዲስ እየጎለበቱ የመጡ ሀገራት አሁን ያለው አለምአቀፍ ስርአት አይጠቅመንም በማለት እንዲቀየር እና እንዲሻሻል ይታገላሉ።
    ምሳሌ፦ BRICS ሀገራት (ቻይና፣ ህንድ፣ ብራዚል ወዘተ) እና ጀርመን አለምአቀፍ ተቋማት የእነሱን ፍላጎት በሚያንጸባርቅ መልኩ እንዲዋቀሩ መታገላቸው።
  • 3. Self-abnegation (የራስን ጥቅም አሳልፎ መስጠት)፦ ድሃ እና በዕርዳታ ላይ ጥገኛ የሆኑ ሀገራት (LDCs) ጊዜያዊ እርዳታ ለማግኘት ሲሉ የረጅም ጊዜ ብሄራዊ ጥቅማቸውን አሳልፈው ይሰጣሉ። ምሳሌ መከረኛው የአፍሪካ ሀገራት

በ Arnold Wolfers ቲዮሪ መሠረት፦ ዶርም ውስጥ አልጋው የተመቸው ተማሪ Self-preservation ነው የሚያደርገው (ማንም እንዳይነካካው!)። ቦታው ያልተመቸው ደግሞ Self-extension በማድረግ ቦታ ለማስቀየር ይሞክራል። ፈተና ደርሶ የጓደኛውን ኖት ለመበደር ሲል የራሱን እራት አሳልፎ የሚሰጥ ተማሪ ደግሞ ቀጥተኛ የ Self-abnegation ምሳሌ ነው! ፕላስ የፍሬሽማን ካፌ ረጅም ሰልፍ ላይ የቆመ ተማሪም ከ Anarchy ጋር ይታገላል!

2.2.4. Foreign Policy Dimensions

The analysis of foreign policy behavior can also be done along a number of specific dimensions, keeping in mind that behavior can change over time and with different style of leaderships and circumstances. These dimensions include Alignment, Scope, and Modus Operandi.

1. Alignment Dimension

Alignment tendencies describe whether national leaders choose to ally with certain countries or to remain neutral. A country’s alignment behavior can vary over time. We can identify three main alignment tendencies:

  • Alliances: Formal agreements to provide mutual military assistance; as such, they carry legal weight and certain benefits as well as risks. Allied countries can pool their military resources, acquire access to foreign bases, and stake out territories that enemies are on notice will be denied them by force if necessary. Yet, an alliance state also risks interference by allies in its domestic affairs and the possibility of being dragged into unwanted conflicts.
  • Neutrality: A stance of formal non-partisanship in world affairs. By keeping a low profile, neutrals may avoid some of the problems associated with alliances, particularly the generating of potential enemies and counter-alliances. However, neutrals must also be aware that if war clouds gather, there may be no one committed to providing a protective military umbrella. Example: Switzerland carried neutrality to an extreme case by refusing membership to the United Nations until 2002. Note that countries can also tilt towards one side without formal alliances (e.g., Israel, which is not a formal ally of U.S., has sided with the U.S. on many issues).
  • Non-alignment: The foreign policy pattern of most developing states during the Cold War. Most developing countries formed the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM), calling for a new foreign policy path disregarding both the West (US) and East (USSR) bloc politics. NAM advocated for South-South cooperation.

Alignment (የግንኙነት ወገንተኝነት)፦ አንድ ሀገር ከሌሎች ሀገራት ጋር የሚኖረው የወታደራዊና የፖለቲካ ጥምረት ወገንተኝነት ነው። በ 3 ይከፈላል፦

  • Alliances (ወታደራዊ ጥምረት)፦ በህግ የተደገፈ የጋራ ወታደራዊ እርዳታ ስምምነት። ጥቅሙ፦ የጦር ሀይል ማጣመርና ጥበቃ ማግኘት ሲሆን፤ ጉዳቱ፦ በሀገር ውስጥ ጉዳይ ጣልቃ መግባትና ባልተፈለገ ጦርነት ውስጥ መጎተት ነው።
  • Neutrality (ገለልተኝነት)፦ በአለም አቀፍ ግጭቶች ውስጥ ማንንም አለመደገፍ።
    ምሳሌ፦ ስዊዘርላንድ (Switzerland) እስከ 2002 ድረስ የ UN አባል እንኳ ሳትሆን ከፍተኛ ገለልተኝነትን አሳይታለች። ኢስራኤል ከአሜሪካ ጋር ይፋዊ የወታደራዊ ውል (formal alliance) ባይኖራትም በብዙ ነገሮች አሜሪካን ትደግፋለች።
  • Non-alignment (ያልተሰለፉ ሀገራት ንቅናቄ - NAM)፦ በቀዝቃዛው ጦርነት (Cold War) ወቅት ታዳጊ ሀገራት በምዕራቡ (አሜሪካ) እና በምስራቁ (ሶቪየት ህብረት) ጎራ ሳልሰለፍ የራሴን መንገድ እከተላለሁ በማለት የፈጠሩት ንቅናቄ ነው።

2. Scope Dimension

Scope refers to the extent or geographic reach of a country's foreign policy activities and interests. Based on scope, states can be categorized as:

  • Global Actors: Major powers that define their interest in global terms, interacting regularly with countries in nearly every region of the world. They have the capability and wherewithal to influence world events.
    Examples: USA (maintains military and diplomatic presence globally). Historically, USSR. China is rapidly expanding its global presence (especially via investments in Africa).
  • Regional Actors: Countries that interact primarily with neighboring states in their same geographical area, except for economic trade with major global powers.
    Examples: South Africa in Africa / Southern Africa (SADC, AU); India in South Asia.
  • Isolationism: A policy of minimal involvement in international affairs, usually caused by key weaknesses or geographic remoteness.
    Examples: Burma (Myanmar) in the 1960s and 1970s. Note: USA, China, and ex-USSR all passed through periods of relative isolationism before becoming global actors.

Scope (የስፋት/የአድማስ ወሰን)፦ የሀገሪቱ የውጭ ፖሊሲ እንቅስቃሴ እስከየት ድረስ እንደሚዘልቅ ያሳያል።

  • Global Actors፦ በመላው አለም ላይ ተፅዕኖ ማሳደር የሚችሉ (ለምሳሌ፡ አሜሪካ፣ ቻይና)።
  • Regional Actors፦ በራሳቸው ክልል/ቀጠና ብቻ ትኩረት የሚያደርጉ (ለምሳሌ፡ ደቡብ አፍሪካ በ SADC/AU፣ ህንድ በደቡብ እስያ)።
  • Isolationism (ብቸኝነት/መገለል)፦ ከውጭ አለም ጋር ግንኙነትን መቀነስ።
    ምሳሌ፦ በ 1960 ዎቹ እና 70 ዎቹ በርማ (Burma) የተከተለችው ፖሊሲ።

3. Mode of Operation / "Modus Operandi"

Modus operandi describes the method of operation states choose to address international issues.

  • Multilateral Approach: Relying on international forums, multilateral institutions, and collective bargaining (e.g., United Nations) to solve problems. It enhances collective bargaining power for smaller or developing states and reduces the cost of establishing multiple bilateral embassies.
    Examples: Germany (despite its economic power, is known to be multilateralist) and most Scandinavian countries. Most developing countries also prefer multilateralism.
  • Unilateral Approach: Relying on one's own economic and military power to settle issues independently without relying on international bodies. Unilateral states often use "carrot and stick" diplomacy, intervention, and the threat or use of force. Stronger powers are more likely to initiate unilateral actions.

📌 Modus Operandi (የአሰራር ስልት)፦ ሀገራት ችግሮችን ለመፍታት የሚጠቀሙበት መንገድ።

  • Multilateralism (ብዙ ወገንተኝነት)፦ እንደ UN ባሉ አለምአቀፍ ተቋማት በጋራ መስራት። ለድሃ ሀገራት አምባሲ የማቋቋም ወጪን ይቀንሳል።
    ምሳሌ፦ ጀርመን (Germany) እና የስካንዲኔቪያን ሀገራት (Scandinavian countries)።
  • Unilateralism (አንድ ወገንተኝነት)፦ የራስን ወታደራዊና ኢኮኖሚያዊ ጉልበት ተጠቅሞ በብቸኝነት እርምጃ መውሰድ (Carrot and Stick diplomacy መጠቀም)።
💡 Exam Hint:
Matching Question Alert!
- Neutrality Extreme Example = Switzerland (until 2002)
- Isolationism Example = Burma (1960s-1970s)
- Multilateralism Example = Germany & Scandinavian Countries
- Regional Actor Example = South Africa & India

2.2.5. Instruments of Foreign Policy

To achieve their foreign policy objectives, states employ various instruments. The main instruments discussed are Diplomacy and Economic Instruments.

A. Diplomacy

Definition & Nature:
Diplomacy has existed for thousands of years (at least 2,500 years of recorded envoy travel). It is defined as a process between actors (diplomats representing states) who engage in private and public dialogue to pursue their objectives peacefully.
Crucial Distinction: Diplomacy is NOT foreign policy! Diplomacy is a tool/instrument of foreign policy used to execute foreign policy goals.

Evolution of Diplomacy:
In the past, diplomacy was rigid, formalistic, secret, and strictly bilateral (conducted by ambassadors in foreign soil). Modern diplomacy (post-WWI and League of Nations/UN era) transformed into multilateral diplomacy, public diplomacy, and summitry diplomacy (leader-to-leader). Governed by the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations (1961). Note that modern diplomacy also involves non-state actors like IGOs (UN, EU) and INGOs (Greenpeace).

Diplomatic Bargaining & Tactics:
Bargaining is a means of settling differences over priorities through proposal exchanges. States use "Carrot and Stick" approaches:

  • The Stick Approach: Threats and Punishments (Threats are hypothetical actions; punishments are actual actions).
  • The Carrot Approach: Promises and Rewards (Promises are hypothetical future rewards; rewards are actual actions/concessions given).

Rules of Effective Diplomacy:

  1. Be realistic: Match goals with the ability to achieve them.
  2. Be careful about what you say: Plan and weigh words carefully.
  3. Seek common ground: Negotiation involves concession; maintain flexibility.
  4. Understand the other side: Appreciate opponent's perspective.
  5. Be patient: Avoid rash concessions due to anxiety.
  6. Leave avenues of retreat open: Do not trap opponents in a corner; allow them an "out" to save face/prestige.

ዲፕሎማሲ (Diplomacy)፦ ሀገራት በሰላማዊ መንገድ ውይይት በማድረግ ፍላጎታቸውን የሚያስፈጽሙበት የውጭ ፖሊሲ መሳሪያ ነው።
⚠️ ትልቅ ማስታወሻ፦ ዲፕሎማሲ እና የውጭ ፖሊሲ አንድ አይደሉም! ዲፕሎማሲ የውጭ ፖሊሲ ማስፈጸሚያ መሣሪያ (Tool) ነው።

👉 Carrot and Stick Strategy (የማባበያ እና የማስፈራሪያ ስልት)፦

  • Stick (በትር/ቀጣይ)፦ ማስፈራሪያ (Threat) እና ቅጣት (Punishment)።
  • Carrot (ካሮት/ማባበያ)፦ ቃል መግባት (Promise) እና ሽልማት/ጥቅም መስጠት (Reward)።

👉 ውጤታማ የዲፕሎማሲ ህጎች (Rules of Effective Diplomacy)፦ ሀቅን መጋፈጥ (Be realistic)፣ ንግግርን መንቀስ (Be careful)፣ የጋራ መግባቢያ መፈለግ፣ የሌላውን ወገን ሀሳብ መረዳት፣ ታጋሽ መሆን፣ እና ለተቃራኒ ወገን ማመልጫ/ክብር ማስጠበቂያ መንገድ መተው (Leave avenues of retreat open)።

B. Economic Instruments of Foreign Policy

Modern states are economically interdependent. Holsti states that economic/trade instruments are used for three main purposes:

  1. To achieve foreign policy objectives by exploiting need/dependence and offering rewards or punishments.
  2. To increase a state's capability or deprive a potential enemy's capabilities.
  3. To create economic satellites or maintain political obedience.

Conditions for Effectiveness: Economic instruments work ONLY IF:

  • The target state perceives a genuine need for the reward or avoidance of punishment.
  • No alternative market or supply source is easily available to the target state.

Specific Economic Techniques (Control over flow of goods & capital):

InstrumentExplanationየአማርኛ ማብራሪያ
TariffTax imposed on foreign goods coming into a country to raise revenue or protect domestic producers. Manipulated up/down as reward or punishment.ከውጭ በሚገቡ እቃዎች ላይ የሚጣል ቀረጥ/ታክስ። ታክሱን በመጨመር ወይም በመቀነስ ሀገራትን መቅጣት ወይም ማበረታታት ይቻላል።
QuotaEstablishing strict limit on the quantity/amount of specific imported commodities allowed into a country within a given period.ወደ ሀገር ውስጥ በሚገቡ እቃዎች መጠን ላይ ገደብ (ኮታ) መጣል።
BoycottA trade restriction organized by a government that eliminates the import of specific commodities or total export products from a targeted country. Importers must secure licenses.መንግስት የተወሰነ ሀገር እቃ እንዳይገባ ወይም እንዳይሸጥ የሚያደርገው ይፋዊ የንግድ እቀባ/እግድ።
EmbargoProhibiting domestic businessmen/commercial organizations from engaging in trade transactions with a target country (often on strategic materials or total goods).ዜጎች እና ነጋዴዎች ከተቀጣችው ሀገር ጋር ምንም አይነት የንግድ ግንኙነት እንዳያደርጉ በህግ ሙሉ በሙሉ ማገድ።
Loans, Credits & Currency ManipulationsOffering favorable loan rates, credit extension, or manipulating exchange rates to grant favorable terms of trade or reward developing states.ብድር መስጠት፣ የብድር ጊዜ ማራዘም ወይም የምንዛሬ ተመንን በመቀየር ለወዳጅ ሀገር ጥቅም መስጠት።
Foreign AidTransfer of money, goods, or technical advice from donor to recipient. Includes military aid, technical assistance, grants, commodity programs, and development loans. Tied with political/economic conditions.የገንዘብ፣ የእቃ ወይም የቴክኒክ እርዳታ መስጠት። እርዳታ አብዛኛውን ጊዜ ከፖለቲካዊ እና ኢኮኖሚያዊ ቅድመ-ሁኔታዎች (strings attached) ጋር የተያያዘ ነው።
Military AidThe oldest type of aid used for buttressing alliances. Example: US and USSR military aid programs during Cold War; US military aid to Saudi Arabia and Iran in late 1960s/1970s.ወታደራዊ መሳሪያ እና ድጋፍ መስጠት። ምሳሌ፦ አሜሪካ ለሳዑዲ አረቢያ እና ኢራን የሰጠችው በቢሊዮን የሚቆጠር ወታደራዊ እርዳታ።
